reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents a creator-run subscriber-milestone giveaway for one $50 Nike gift card, identified as closed in the title. Participation involves commenting the creator's city and state and providing an external contact method, with correct entries described as entering a randomizer for one winner. The contact-information request is presented as contest administration, and no payment demand, credential request, deceptive claim, delivery outcome, or connection between subscription prompts and a financial offer is described.

citations.quote: Now for my 500 subscriber giveaway, I want to give away a $50 Nike gift card. I have yet to pick up the gift card, but I will soon.

To enter you must comment in the comment section below what city and state I live in. No abbreviations. Type out the city and state. Also leave a way for me to contact you such as Instagram, Twitter, Gmail etc..
All correct entries will be put into a randomizer and winner will be chosen on Sunday February 26, 2017. 1 entry per person.
Nike Gift Card Giveaway (CLOSED)

opening.argument: The offer is explicitly conditional on a viewer performing several actions: submit the creator's city and state, provide an external contact method, and participate through the channel's audience funnel. In exchange, one selected entrant is promised a $50 Nike gift card. That is a low-barrier reward tied to information submission and contact access, not simply an unsolicited gift. The process also leaves the promised asset unresolved because the speaker says he had not yet obtained the gift card. The combination of an attractive reward and required viewer action is sufficient to treat this as a solicitation for participation in a purported reward flow.

citations.quote: I am giving away a $50 Nike Gift card in celebration of this channel reaching 500 subscribers.

To enter you must comment in the comment section below what city and state I live in. No abbreviations. Type out the city and state. Also leave a way for me to contact you such as Instagram, Twitter, Gmail etc..
I have yet to pick up the gift card, but I will soon.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the requested information “contest administration” does not remove the central exchange: viewers are asked to submit an answer and an off-platform contact route to pursue a promised gift card. The stated randomizer describes a selection mechanism, but it does not establish that the reward exists or will be delivered. The title's “CLOSED” label likewise says nothing about whether the solicitation was genuine while active.

citations.quote: To enter you must comment in the comment section below what city and state I live in.
I have yet to pick up the gift card, but I will soon.
Nike Gift Card Giveaway (CLOSED)

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The cited material shows a normal, bounded giveaway rather than a deceptive acquisition scheme. The required entry is a city-and-state answer, while the external contact method is offered so the organizer can reach a winner. The speaker expressly limits entries and describes a random selection, but nothing shows payment, credentials, or an obligation to buy. Saying the card had not yet been picked up does not show that it would not be obtained.

citations.quote: All correct entries will be put into a randomizer and winner will be chosen on Sunday February 26, 2017. 1 entry per person.
there's one entry per person
Also leave a way for me to contact you such as Instagram, Twitter, Gmail etc..

opening.argument: Several risk signals appear together: a cash-equivalent $50 gift card, a simple knowledge-based entry, a request for an Instagram, Twitter, Gmail, or other external contact route, and a fixed deadline followed by a promised winner announcement. The reward is framed as easy to obtain, while the organizer admits the gift card has not yet been purchased. This combination creates urgency and shifts viewers toward sharing contact information before the underlying prize is secured. The description also includes a shortened external link, adding another off-platform path around the promotion.

citations.quote: I want to give away a $50 Nike gift card.
please if you could leave a way for me to contact you leave your Instagram or your Twitter or Gmail or something something outside of YouTube
The contest will end on Saturday February 25, 2017.
http://bit.ly/1Z7svNm
I have yet to pick up the gift card, but I will soon.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats each signal in isolation. A deadline, a promised announcement, a shortened link, and external contact requests operate together as a funnel for engagement and data collection, while the prize is still unsecured. “Randomizer” describes how a name might be selected; it does not verify funding, delivery, or identity of the organizer. A claim that no payment was demanded overlooks that scam-like acquisition can begin with low-cost contact harvesting.

citations.quote: The contest will end on Saturday February 25, 2017.
http://bit.ly/1Z7svNm
I have yet to pick up the gift card, but I will soon.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These are ordinary contest mechanics, not evidence of deception. The deadline is paired with a stated end date and winner date, and the entry is limited to one per person. The link is presented as a subscription link, not as a payment or verification page. Most importantly, the evidence contains no request for money, passwords, or financial credentials; an external contact method alone does not establish harmful data collection.

citations.quote: All correct entries will be put into a randomizer and winner will be chosen on Sunday February 26, 2017. 1 entry per person.
PLEASE CLICK HERE TO SUBSCRIBE AND ENJOY THIS JOURNEY WITH ME!
Also leave a way for me to contact you such as Instagram, Twitter, Gmail etc..

opening.argument: Although presented as appreciation for subscribers, the video functions as a promotional acquisition campaign. The reward is explicitly tied to a subscriber milestone, viewers are directed to comment and provide off-platform contact details, and the description separately urges them to subscribe. The ending frame reinforces that promotional role with social handles and large “SUBSCRIBE” prompts. Thus the gift card is not merely an ordinary reward; it is the incentive used to steer viewers into the creator's audience and external-contact network. The promotional framing does not prove fulfillment, and the offer remains a reward linked to viewer action.

citations.quote: Just one week later and are already…as of now, as I'm filming this at 808 subscribers.
PLEASE CLICK HERE TO SUBSCRIBE AND ENJOY THIS JOURNEY WITH ME!
Also leave a way for me to contact you such as Instagram, Twitter, Gmail etc..

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense's description of a giveaway does not answer the promotional function. The offer is introduced because of subscriber growth, accompanied by a direct subscription instruction, and paired with off-platform contact collection. Calling that “appreciation” is a favorable characterization, not proof that the promised card was secured or that the funnel was harmless. The visible subscription and social prompts reinforce that viewers are being steered, not merely informed.

citations.quote: I am giving away a $50 Nike Gift card in celebration of this channel reaching 500 subscribers.
PLEASE CLICK HERE TO SUBSCRIBE AND ENJOY THIS JOURNEY WITH ME!

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Promotion and fraud are not interchangeable. Reaching a subscriber milestone explains why the creator offers the giveaway, while the entry instructions specify a city-and-state answer and one entry per person. The closing frame's social and subscription prompts show channel promotion, but they do not show a false prize, payment demand, or deceptive outcome. The prosecution's conclusion depends on treating ordinary audience-building as proof of a scam.
